comments.author: RebarBotNava
comments.body: S1 ee8a plan-review: BLOCK on G6 (major, impact 0.67) — plan cited mcp_servers' resolution shape, which silently degrades malformed JSON to {}, while also demanding fail-loud for unset ${env:VAR}; malformed headers JSON was unspecified. Remediated: headers now explicitly raises LLMConfigError on malformed JSON in any layer (diverging from mcp_servers, with reason stated), plus a failure-path test and an AC. Re-reviewing.

comments.author: RebarBotNava
comments.body: S2 6cd0 plan-review: BLOCK x3 — E2 (run_id provenance unspecified), G6 CRITICAL (plan named runner.py:259/:719 but not the seam; :259 is inside FakeRunner.run which has no instance config, reaching config only via req.config), T8 CRITICAL (schema trace_id descriptions still say 'Langfuse trace id when tracing is enabled', contradicting the new emitted semantics). All three verified against the tree. Remediated: dropped run_id entirely (no distinct consumer; trace_id identifies the run), named req.config.trace_id as the seam with operations.py:209-212 provenance and the dataclasses.replace/max_output_cfg survival note, added both schema files to Scope with description updates and two new ACs. Propagated the run_id removal to the epic, 26ae and 98b6.

comments.author: RebarBotNava
comments.body: S1 ee8a re-review: BLOCK on G6 CRITICAL (impact 1.0) — validation ordering unspecified; if CR/LF/NUL checks run before ${env:VAR} substitution, an env var containing CRLF bypasses the injection guard (concrete scenario: value '${env:GATEWAY_TAG}' with GATEWAY_TAG='foo\\r\\nInjected: bar'). This is a real header-injection hole in the feature whose purpose is preventing it. Remediated: substitution runs first and every check applies to the fully resolved value, with a parametrized ordering regression test and an AC. Propagated the same rule to 26ae, whose ${run:...} substitution happens later at call time, so validation is re-applied on the substituted result there too.

comments.author: RebarBotNava
comments.body: S2 6cd0 re-review: PASS, attestation certified at 95387192. Applied 3 critical advisories rather than claiming on the PASS: E5 (completion-verifier boundary gate_dispatch:762 / runner:719 / completion_verdict.schema.json all in scope but every schema-naming AC named only review_result.schema.json — half the changed surface had no acceptance coverage), E1+A1 (ticket_id and operation minted with no named consumer or covering AC). Added ACs for both gate surfaces and for ticket_id/operation, named 26ae as their downstream consumer, and added a both-boundaries testing note. This invalidates the attestation; re-reviewing.

comments.author: RebarBotNava
comments.body: S1 ee8a third review: BLOCK on T8 CRITICAL — the ${...} grammar left every non-${env:} form undispositioned: whether ${run:...} is validated as a literal/skipped/deferred, and whether an unrecognized namespace or malformed placeholder is a hard error or a silent literal. Direct consequence of the previous ordering fix ('validate the resolved value' is incoherent for values that cannot be resolved yet). Remediated: closed two-namespace grammar owned by headers.py including the ${run:} key vocabulary as a module constant (no dependency on 6cd0), every malformed/unknown form a hard LLMConfigError, ${run:} left unresolved but key-checked at config time, value validation on the post-env value with placeholders intact and re-run after ${run:} substitution in 26ae. Added 2 ACs and grammar-disposition tests.

comments.author: RebarBotNava
comments.body: S2 6cd0 third review: BLOCK x2 CRITICAL (G1G2 + G6, same defect) — plan named runner.py:259 and :719 but omitted :254, the FakeRunner mode=='structured' branch, which also hardcodes trace_id=None and does not read req.config. Source comment at :239 reads 'Structured mode (e.g. verify_completion)', so the completion verifier returns from :254; the completion-path AC added in the previous round would have been unsatisfiable against the fake runner. Verified in tree. Remediated: all three sites now named with the req.mode branch-selection rationale.

comments.author: RebarBotNava
comments.body: S2 6cd0: BLOCK G6 CRITICAL — restated schema wording 'present inside any gate run' would be FALSE: grep found 7 trace_id:None emitters, not 3. completion_verdict_assembly.py:153, completion_reconcile.py:252 and completion_failures.py:98 emit verdicts inside the completion gate scope without touching the runner; spec_scan.py:138 is not a gate op. comments.author: RebarBotNava

comments.author: RebarBotNava
comments.body: S1 ee8a: BLOCK G6 CRITICAL — fail-loud malformed-JSON contract named only env and CLI, but config.py:585-594 shows the file table also accepts a JSON string and silently degrades it to {}. Verified. Remediated: all three layers raise, and the file layer's accepted shapes are pinned (native TOML table or JSON string; neither-shape or non-object JSON is a hard error), with 2 ACs and testing coverage for all three layers.

comments.author: RebarBotNava
comments.body: Epic 7e9e: BLOCK x2 CRITICAL. E2 — criterion 6 promised 'parametrized tests over the rejected set' without enumerating it; now names the five header names and CR/LF/NUL explicitly. T8 — REAL DESIGN GAP: no fallback specified for an absent ${run:...} substituend. Verified only two production gate_config scopes exist (gate_dispatch:167, :762); code-review, named as a gate op in the epic's own Context, opens none and has no ticket, so ${run:trace_id}/${run:ticket_id} are absent there. Decided: omit the whole header rather than send empty or raise — an empty correlation header pollutes the gateway, and raising would break standalone ops merely because headers are globally configured (observability must never break an operation). Asymmetry with unset-${env:VAR}-raises is deliberate and now stated: env absence is a config mistake, run absence is legitimate runtime context. Applied to 26ae + epic.

comments.author: RebarBotNava
comments.body: Epic 7e9e: BLOCK x3 CRITICAL. T1+T3 demanded empirical proof that ModelSettings.extra_headers reaches the wire through rebar's OWN provider path rather than a docs claim. RAN THE SPIKE: pinned pydantic-ai 1.107.2; settings.py declares extra_headers dict[str,str]; models/openai.py reads :1001 forwards :1034; drove ProviderSession.model_for('openai:gpt-4o') with base_url through _build_openai/_RebarOpenAICompatibleProvider, intercepting at the httpx.AsyncHTTPTransport seam providers.py documents. RESULT: request hit <base_url>/chat/completions with x-litellm-trace-id and x-corp-tag both verbatim on the wire and Authorization: Bearer k intact. Capability verified, auth-preservation confirmed. Recorded in the epic with citations. Also fixed COH/E1: criterion 7 (omit-on-absent-substituend) now assigned to the delivery child. Incidental: pydantic-ai deprecation warning — 'openai:' resolves to Responses API in v2.0, use 'openai-chat:'; out of scope, noting for later.

comments.author: RebarBotNava
comments.body: Epic 7e9e PASS certified at 537456586. comments.author: RebarBotNava
comments.body: Epic 7e9e: BLOCK T8 CRITICAL — ${run:operation} declared in the closed vocabulary but its VALUE SET was never enumerated, and the epic's prose said 'code-review' where rebar's canonical identifier is 'review-code'. A vocabulary mismatch would emit wrong header values. Remediated across three tickets: operation now resolves to exactly review-plan | verify-completion (rebar's CLI verb names, not invented spellings like plan_review); review-code explicitly absent because it opens no gate scope, which is why the omit rule exists; identifier corrected in epic criterion 7, 6cd0's literals and ACs, and 26ae's prose. Re-reviewing 6cd0 then the epic in dependency order.

comments.author: RebarBotNava
comments.body: PRIOR-ART CONFORMANCE CHECK complete. Verdicts: D1 CONFORMS, D2 CONFORMS, D3a CONFORMS, D3b DIVERGES-JUSTIFIED, D4 DIVERGES-JUSTIFIED, D6 DIVERGES-FIX. Applied revisions across all five tickets: (1) D6 — trace_id now DERIVED from the active recording OTel span, minting only as fallback, because tracing.py:196 already exports rebar OTLP spans to Langfuse and an unrelated random id would split one run into two traces; (2) D1 — mandatory fresh dict() copy per call: VERIFIED LIVE that pinned pydantic-ai 1.107.2 models/openai.py:1001 reads extra_headers with no copy then :1002 setdefault mutates the caller's dict (upstream bug 6866; Responses :2300 and anthropic :772 both copy) — would have polluted rebar's config dict and leaked a pydantic-ai version string into signed provenance; (3) merge-precedence pin test, the most-regressed behaviour in comparable projects; (4) $$ escape for a literal ${; (5) rejection message names llm.api_key (Prometheus ReservedHeaders precedent: a denylist is legitimate when a first-class auth channel exists); (6) CORRECTION — extra_headers is INERT on Bedrock at this pin (zero refs in models/bedrock.py) despite settings.py listing it; epic claim corrected and 98b6 documents it.

comments.author: RebarBotNava
comments.body: S2 6cd0: BLOCK G7 CRITICAL — genuine parent/child conflict. The D6 conformance fix made the child derive trace_id from the active OTel span, which the epic's Out-of-scope explicitly excluded ('no unification of rebar's own OTLP spans with the gateway's records'). Applied realign-to-parent: the PARENT was wrong — the conformance check showed sharing the id is required for the stated goal, not optional. Epic scope narrowed to what is genuinely still excluded (no rebar-owned root span, no traceparent injection); id-sharing moved explicitly in scope with rationale. Re-reviewing S2 then the epic.

comments.author: RebarBotNava
comments.body: Epic 7e9e: BLOCK G6 CRITICAL — the D6 in-scope claim (reading the active OTel span aligns the gateway header with rebar's exported Langfuse spans) is NOT achieved at the described read point. rebar opens no root span, so at the gate boundary nothing is recording and the id mints; tracing.py's per-candidate spans open later inside each model request, each its own trace root, so their trace_ids never equal the header value under fan-out. Claim corrected in epic + 6cd0 rather than reverting the read: reading an existing span is still correct and free when an enclosing span exists, but the epic now states plainly that header/span alignment requires the run-level root span and is the deferred follow-on. This reconciles the conformance finding with the user's B1-now/B2-later scope.
